title: State of the Union: Why Local, Why Now — NVIDIA, Osmantic, Roboflow, EXO Labs, @matthew_berman
talk_summary: A panel of local-AI founders and NVIDIA discuss why running models locally is now viable: better open models, better harnesses, and multimodel routing. The only concrete, transferable engineering content is the pattern of using frontier models to plan and cheaper/specialized models to execute, plus distilling a big model's outputs into a small specialized model for a narrow task.

takeaways.what_they_do: Route the top-level planning/architecture to the most capable (expensive) model, then hand subtasks to cheaper workhorse or local models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let the top model plan uh the the architecture whatever the kind of top level plan is and then the actual execution of the code can go to uh a more reasonably priced smaller model

takeaways.technique: Distill frontier outputs into a narrow specialized model
takeaways.what_they_do: Use large models plus an LLM-as-judge consensus pass to label a domain dataset, then train/run a small specialized model for the narrow task in production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use LMS as judge to say hey we agree with some amount of consensus and now we have a specialized data set then we can use that specific model

takeaways.what_they_do: Run multiple models over the same input and use an LLM judge to keep only agreed-upon outputs as a trusted dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have those maybe all have a pass at understanding something use LMS as judge to say hey we agree with some amount of consensus

takeaways.what_they_do: Argue the pendulum has swung from one general model to many specialized models tuned per use case/workflow, with routing between them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: small and specialized models are the future and it is going to be very user by per use case per workflow

takeaways.technique: Tune existing stack for the target hardware rather than inventing
takeaways.what_they_do: Got 10x perf by assembling already-solved NVIDIA optimizations (quantization, inference backend, config tuning) for the smaller device, not new CS.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we didn't solve any new computer science to do this. We actually took things that the experts at NVIDIA had already solved
